overview.headline: How air density, speed and shape create drag force

keyPoints.point: Students learn that drag increases with air density and the square of velocity.
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity

keyPoints.point: Students learn to calculate drag from coefficient, density, velocity and area.
keyPoints.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ)

keyPoints.point: Students learn that reference area choice changes the coefficient but not the drag.
keyPoints.quote: If we choose the wing area, rather than the cross-sectional area, the computed coefficient will have a different value.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that drag coefficients are found experimentally and include several drag sources.
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyTerms.gloss: Single variable that collects complex shape and flow effects for drag
keyTerms.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyTerms.gloss: Chosen area size used to characterize aerodynamic force dependence
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: Mass per volume of air represented by rho in the equation
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).
